newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar extends gains by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar extends gains by close.

text.p: White sugar futures extended earlier gains and finished at the highs on Wednesday, although volumes were not spectacular.
Nearby December futures ended $1.40 higher at $324.00 a tonne, well off the day's low of $321.50. March also rose $1.40 to finish at the day's peak of $320.50. Turnover was 1,588 lots.
The London market failed to react to the day's physical news -- the results of two buying tenders from Tunisia and Jordan.
Tunisia bought a cargo of 45 ICUMSA white sugar for shipment in June 1997 after an earlier snap tender.
Traders said the price paid was $356.50 per tonne c & f, although London sources said earlier the price was $354.50.
Jordan bought 30,000 tonnes of whites in two lots for shipment starting in mid-November from Louis Dreyfus.
One lot of 15,000 tonnes second half November shipment was bought at $367 per tonne c & f, with the rest for shipment in the first half of December and bought at $360.50.
The result of Syria's and Sri Lanka's tenders are not expected until Thursday.
In its weekly tender, the European Union awarded a total 97,750 tonnes of current series white sugar with an export rebate of a maximum 45.064 Ecus per 100 kilos.
The Paris market was slow, with December finishing 20 cents higher at $324.20 and March gaining 50 cents to $320.50.
